name: Play Customer Promo Video
description: Fetch and play a customer-hosted video, audio or image asset locally over X11. Identifies the media URLs on a page, downloads them with an HTTP status check, validates the file (size, magic bytes, ffprobe, player availability), then starts the player detached and confirms the process is alive.
workflow: IDENTIFY: list the media URLs on the page with curl and a grep for src/href ending in mp4, webm, mov, jpg, png or mp3.
DOWNLOAD: fetch the asset with curl -sSL -o <asset> <url> and read the HTTP status, size and content type from the -w format string.
VALIDATE: run ./verify.sh <asset> — seven checks: size, magic bytes, ffprobe, X11 display, player availability, readability.
PLAY: run ./play.sh <asset>; it auto-detects the player, detaches with setsid and writes the log to /tmp/<player>-skill-<pid>.log.
CONFIRM: check for the player process with pgrep. No PID after 3s means read the log with cat.
promptHints: Player hierarchy is mpv, then vlc, then ffplay, then parole.
cd $(dirname <asset>) before setsid — absolute paths through ~ do not always resolve in memphis_exec.
The exec shell is /bin/sh, not bash: judge success by ps/pgrep, not by the exit code of the backgrounded command.
Do NOT use nohup cmd & — the parent shell dies with the exec. setsid -f cmd with </dev/null is the correct detach.

examples.outcome: The skill identifies the asset, downloads it with a status check, validates it with verify.sh, starts the player detached and confirms the process is running.

notes: Limits: no authenticated or CDN downloads, no HLS/DASH streams, no upload, no transcoding, and no touch of sudo, services or boot.
Runtime quirk recorded on this host: mpv is not installed; the fallback chain is what makes the skill work.
verify.sh v1.1 distinguishes the container kind before checking stream types — v1.0 reported a false-positive video stream for static JPEG files.
